title: Integrator Dawn — mini onramp journal
body:
Purpose:
This is a working journal for the Integrator persona (platform engineers & integrators who embed Redwood SDKs into larger products). Codename: 'Dawn'. The goal is a tiny, gated onramp that produces: 1) a 3-minute success path (hello world call), 2) a 10-minute smoke-lab (telemetry + basic feature flagging), and 3) an instrumented rollback/diagnostic checklist for field engineers.

Audience:
- Integrators (internal and external)
- Solutions engineers running quick POC installs
- DevEx engineers owning the starter kit and telemetry hooks

Constraints / design decisions (early):
- Zero infra changes required to run the mini-lab (use hosted API creds by default).
- Minimal dependencies: single Python + shell script set.
- Provide feature-flag toggles for: routing policy (cost vs latency), KV cache enabled, and quantization profile suggestion.
- Telemetry events must be emitted in-binary (protobuf) and human-readable JSON for early debugging.

3-minute success path (for demo):
1) clone: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/integrator-dawn-starter.git
2) cd integrator-dawn-starter && pip install -r requirements.txt
3) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-prod-XXXXX
4) python hello_inference.py --model "redwood/fast-text-1" --prompt "Summarize: ..."
Expected: one streaming response printed, latency < 300ms for short prompts when run from us-west.

10-minute smoke-lab (step-by-step):
- Setup (2 min): confirm API key, run local env check (scripts/env_check.sh)
- Instrument (3 min): enable telemetry (export REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=on) and open telemetry viewer: http://localhost:8000/telemetry (local shim)
- Run scenario (3 min): run ./smoke/run_scenarios.sh --cases basic-generation,cache-hit,high-latency-fallback
- Validate (2 min): check telemetry for events: request.start, kernel.select, response.streamed, fallback.used

Quick smoke scripts (put in /smoke):
- curl example (basic generation):
  curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"redwood/fast-text-1","input":"Write a 2-line haiku about coffee."}'

- small shell test: smoke/check_latency.sh
  (runs 10 requests, prints p50/p95, flags >500ms)

Telemetry events to collect (minimum):
- request.start (tags: model, route, client_id)
- kernel.select (tags: model_variant, quant_profile, gpu_type)
- batch.size (value)
- kvcache.hit_ratio (value)
- response.streamed (tokens_sent)
- fallback.invoked (reason)
- rollout.flag (flag_name, new_value)
- error.rate (error_code)
Notes: attach sample protobuf schema in repo under /telemetry/schema.proto (TODO: finalize names).

Gating checklist before recommending Dedicated/private install: (for Solutions Eng)
- Successful end-to-end flows with telemetry enabled for 1 day of synthetic load.
- Smoke tests: p95 < 1s for standard prompt mix.
- Feature flags work: routing policy flips to 'cost' and 'latency' with measurable difference.
- Failover validated: simulated partial region outage triggers fallback to secondary model variant.
- Rollout safety: can revert flag in < 30s and DB entries for rollout are auditable.

Troubleshooting quick wins (notes to self):
- If curl returns 401: check REDWOOD_API_KEY scoping (tokens for demo vs prod).
- If streaming stalls at 0.0 tokens: enable TRACE=1 and look for kvcache mismatch (common with local mock).
- If p95 > 1s: ensure batching not accidentally increased (check BATCH_SIZE env).

Unresolved questions / TODOs (open items):
- Decide default quantization recommendation for small CPU-backed dev boxes (int8 vs gf16).
- Confirm telemetry retention policy for quickstart (logs vs metrics).
- Add a tiny Web UI for non-engineer integrators (MVP: show last 50 telemetry events).
- Author a one-pager for Sales about integrator quick wins (who to hand off to Solutions).

UX copy snippets (for quickstart README):
- Title: "Integrator Dawn: from clone to first inference in under 3 minutes"
- Blurb: "A step-by-step starter for platform teams who embed Redwood SDKs into larger stacks. Includes telemetry-ready smoke tests and rollback playbooks."
- Callouts: "No infra changes — runs against hosted API by default"

Meeting notes (2024-09-24):
- Attendees: Asha, Mason, Diego, Priya
- Decisions: keep Python-first starter (most integrators comfortable), add node sample later if adoption warrants.
- Action items: Mason to implement smoke scripts (due 2024-10-04), Priya to draft telemetry schema (due 2024-10-01), Diego to wire local telemetry viewer (due 2024-10-07).

Next steps (this journal):
- Finalize README + 3-min path (owner: Asha)
- Land initial smoke scripts and CI flake (owner: Mason)
- Telemetry schema draft v0.1 (owner: Priya)
- Playground demo (10-min script + small web UI) prototype (owner: Diego)

Notes-to-self: keep language blunt and action-focused, expect many small edits from Solutions Eng during first 10 pilots. Capture feedback as issues in the starter repo and tag them with 'integrator-dawn'.

End of journal entry (draft).
